assumptions: Annealing Tm is pydna's primer design model.
limits: No upstream designs tailed primers: the test feeds the products to the graded Golden Gate assembler and checks it rebuilds the templates.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which primers add a Type-IIS site, spacer and chosen overhang to a part on a Tm-matched annealing footprint?

description: Design the PCR primers that ADD Type-IIS fusion sites to a part: enzyme site, spacer and the four-base overhang you chose, on a Tm-matched annealing footprint. This is how a sequence that is not yet a Golden Gate part becomes one, and it is the other half of check_golden_gate_parts — that says which parts are unusable, this makes one usable.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

buffer_bases.description: 5' buffer bases outside the recognition site, so the enzyme has somewhere to sit (NEB recommends 6 nt). Advanced.

enzyme.description: the Type-IIS enzyme the assembly will use.

left_overhang.description: the top-strand overhang to leave at the START of the released part — its length must match the enzyme's own overhang.

right_overhang.description: the top-strand overhang to leave at the END of the released part.

sequence.description: the template to amplify — wire a record, name a library document, or leave unset to use the open record.

target_tm.description: target annealing temperature for the template-binding footprint. In °C.

name: design_fusion_site_primers

forward.description: the forward primer, 5'→3': buffer, recognition site, spacer, your overhang, then the annealing footprint

forwardTm.description: melting temperature of the forward primer's ANNEALING footprint — the tail does not bind the template on the first cycle

product.description: what the pair amplifies, tails included

releasedPart.description: what the enzyme cuts OUT of that product — the part that actually enters the assembly, carrying your two overhangs

reverse.description: the reverse primer, same construction on the other end

reverseTm.description: the same for the reverse primer; the pair is matched, so a gap between these two is the thing to notice
